item.text: Both spoons are at roughly the same room temperature, but your skin senses how quickly heat leaves it, not just an object’s temperature. Metal conducts heat well, so it quickly carries warmth away from your hand into the rest of the spoon. Wood is a poor heat conductor, so heat moves away much more slowly, and the surface touching you warms up. That faster heat loss makes metal feel colder, even though a thermometer would show nearly identical temperatures.
